title: Churn looks catastrophic at 94%, but much of it is a measurement artefact
story: The pipeline's fixed as-of date (2026-08-14) sits well past the dataset's actual last event (2025-10-05), so almost every member reads as churned. Re-anchoring to a data-realistic date drops churn to 84.0%. That is still high, but the 94.0% headline should never be quoted to leadership without this context.
evidence: kpi_01 against kpi_15 in kpi_summary.csv; the PR9 and PR11 as-of decision.
impact: High. Wrong framing risks over-reacting, for example with panic win-back spend, to a partly artefactual number.
action: Report churn with both figures side by side. Treat kpi_15 as the operationally meaningful number.

title: Activation, not renewal, is where the platform loses members
story: Only 18.8% of members log any activity within 7 days of joining. That is an 81.2% drop at a single stage and the largest of any funnel step. No acquisition channel or demographic segment explains it: every Cramér's V is below 0.1.
impact: High. This is the single highest-leverage retention lever found in the dataset.
action: Prioritise onboarding experiments on UX and timing over channel-targeted acquisition spend.

title: Activation is quietly improving, so the funnel is not getting worse
story: Monthly cohort activation rose from about 14.6% in late 2024 to about 36.6% in September 2025. It is the most encouraging non-obvious finding in the dataset and the opposite of what the 81.2% headline drop-off implies in isolation.
impact: Medium. It reframes the story from a broken funnel to an improving one worth investing in.
action: Investigate what changed operationally in early 2025 and double down on it.

title: Churn and activation are platform-wide problems, not a branch-operations issue
story: None of the 40 branches is a statistical churn-rate outlier, and none combines a churn anomaly with bottom-quartile activation. That rules out a few bad branches as the root cause.
evidence: branch_risk_summary.csv (0 of 40 flagged); PR11 section 11.2.2 and PR12 section 12.1(c).
impact: Medium. It redirects the investigation away from branch staffing and operations, toward product and onboarding.
action: Do not fund a branch-level operational audit as a churn fix. Focus centrally on onboarding.

title: A small, well-defined 'paid once, never engaged' cohort is ready for outreach
story: Twelve currently-active members trigger nearly every composite risk signal. Most are single-event members paying 48,000 to 102,000 rupees per logged session. It is a short, actionable list rather than a diffuse population-wide signal.
impact: Medium. The volume is small, but the win-back value per member is high and the targeting cost is low.
action: Reach out directly, by call or PT trial offer, to the 12 flagged members within the next billing cycle.
